approachQuestion.prompt:
Sticky Key Recorder

The strings intended and recorded contain lowercase English letters. A recorder may repeat any intended keystroke one or more times, but may never omit it, insert a different letter, or change the order. Return whether recorded could have been produced from intended in this way. Neither string may be modified.

Constraints: n=intended.length and m=recorded.length, independently in [0,200000]; indexed character access is constant time.

Example 1: intended="book", recorded="bboooookk" -> true.
Example 2: intended="book", recorded="bok" -> false (the two intended o keystrokes cannot shrink).
Example 3: intended="", recorded="a" -> false.
Example 4: intended="", recorded="" -> true.
constraints: Choose the most efficient valid approach for the entire stated input domain; accept equivalent optimal variants.

options.text: Walk through maximal equal-letter runs in both strings together. Each paired run must have the same letter and the recorded run must be at least as long as the intended run. Accept only if both strings exhaust together.
options.feedback: Each intended run can expand, but cannot shrink or exchange letters with another run. These conditions exactly characterize legal repetition.

options.text: Convert both strings to arrays of (letter,count) runs, then compare those arrays for equal letters and recorded counts at least as large.
options.feedback: The run conditions are correct for every input, but storing all run records is unnecessary when the two current runs can be compared immediately.

options.text: Collapse every run to one letter in both strings and compare the collapsed strings.
options.feedback: For intended="book" and recorded="bok", the collapsed strings match, but recorded omitted one required o.

options.text: Accept whenever intended is a subsequence of recorded.
options.feedback: For intended="ab", recorded="acb", intended is a subsequence, but the extra c cannot be created by repeating an intended keystroke.

feedback.reason: Align maximal equal-character runs and enforce a directional multiplicity condition rather than plain equality or membership.
details: At each current pair of indices, reject if the letters differ. Count each full equal-letter run without copying it. Reject if the recorded run is shorter; otherwise advance both to their next run. Finally require both strings to be exhausted.

Each intended equal-letter run must correspond to a recorded run of the same letter with at least its length. Total character counts alone lose run order, and exhausting only one input leaves unmatched recorded or intended content.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method revealed after question 1, choose its tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Use a word-RAM model with constant-time indexed access and signed 64-bit arithmetic. Include all temporary buffers, input copies, and call frames; exclude supplied input and returned output. n and m are independent string lengths. Both scans are iterative and keep no run array, input copies, recursion, hashing, or amortized containers.
constraints: Analyze this fixed method regardless of your answer to question 1; choose the tightest pair.

options.text: O(n + m + 1) time, O(1) auxiliary space
O(n + m + 1) time, O(n + m + 1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Count runs directly while advancing through both strings once.
details: The scans pass each input position at most once. Valid recorded expansions can force both complete scans. Time is O(n+m+1) including empty inputs, and auxiliary state is two indices, two counts, and current letters.

Use a word-RAM model with constant-time indexed access and signed 64-bit arithmetic. Include all temporary buffers, input copies, and call frames; exclude supplied input and returned output. n and m are independent string lengths. Both scans are iterative and keep no run array, input copies, recursion, hashing, or amortized containers.
“O(n + m + 1) time, O(n + m + 1) auxiliary space”: This describes storing every run, which the fixed method avoids.
“O((n + 1)(m + 1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: No run is compared with every run of the other string.
“O(min(n,m) + 1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: One recorded run can be much longer than intended; its full length still has to be checked.
